newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay's unions threaten general strike.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay's unions threaten general strike.

text.p: Paraguay's trade unions warned Tuesday they would call a general strike for early February unless the government came up with an urgent wage proposal.

"If we don't get a specific answer from the government regarding (our request for) a pay rise, we will bring forward protests planned for March," Eduardo Ojeda, leader of the National Workers Center, told reporters.
The unions are demanding staggered wage increases to make up for a 30 percent salary lag against inflation.
"We want a raise of 32 percent...we are willing to negotiate for less, but only in a way that makes wages recover their purchasing power," said Ojeda.

Workers and businessmen Tuesday presented a joint proposal for a rise of 8.2 percent in utilities rates, compensating for 1996 inflation, and a freeze in gasoline prices until March. "We have heard the opinion of the businessmen and the workers and on Wednesday they will get a final proposal from the government," Finance Minister Carlos Facetti said after meeting union and company delegates.
Local media speculated the government would grant a 10 percent raise only to private sector workers.

The unions are demanding salary increases to cope with an average 15 percent rise in gasoline prices, a 14.2 percent rise in electricity, 13.2 percent rise in drinking water services and eight percent rise in cement prices which go into effect Wednesday.
